extracted.intended_audience: developing country governments, accredited entities, project proponents, donors and other stakeholders seeking Green Climate Fund engagement
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance for institutions and project proponents on engaging with the Green Climate Fund (GCF), identifying funding windows and partnership modalities, and aligning proposals with GCF objectives and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCF mission/objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: “GCF is the world’s climate fund for developing countries. We mobilise and deliver capital at scale, strengthen institutions and support transformative change, and bring together partnership networks to deliver impact.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and proposals should demonstrate alignment with GCF’s overarching objectives: mobilising capital at scale, strengthening institutions, supporting transformative change, and leveraging partnerships to deliver measurable impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase access for developing countries
rubrics_metrics.description: “GCF works to increase access for developing countries, which means quicker, simpler, with harmonised standards, delivered closer to local communities, and catalysing more funding.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design proposals and engagement approaches that increase accessibility: simplify procedures where possible, align with harmonised standards, emphasize local delivery/beneficiary reach, and show catalytic potential for mobilising additional finance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify appropriate funding windows and partnership modalities
rubrics_metrics.description: “Explore our funding windows and ways of partnering with us. Access funding.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must select the correct GCF funding window and partnership modality for their activity (e.g., project/programme, specialized facilities). Ensure eligibility and modality fit before preparing full proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project reporting elements (theme, location, partner, value, beneficiaries, emissions avoided)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table headings shown for recently approved projects: Theme; Location; Partner; Total project value; Beneficiaries; Emissions avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and project documents should clearly state thematic alignment, geographic scope, implementing/partner entities, total project value, number and nature of beneficiaries, and expected greenhouse gas emissions reductions/avoidance (with quantification where possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrable local impact and beneficiary outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Project impact stories include beneficiary narratives about livelihood improvements, water savings, increased yields, reliable electricity, and preservation of biodiversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful proposals should present tangible, local-level outcomes (e.g., changes in livelihoods, food security, energy access, ecosystem preservation), supported by evidence or credible theory of change, and include beneficiary perspectives where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation of entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to “GCF new accreditation framework: First window opens for accreditation applications” and links to Accredited Entities / Entity accreditation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities seeking to implement GCF-funded activities typically must obtain GCF accreditation under the applicable framework; applicants should follow accreditation procedures and requirements (see GCF accreditation guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of readiness support and Project Preparation Facility
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick links and content reference Readiness support and Project Preparation Facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries and entities can use readiness financing and the Project Preparation Facility (PPF) to build capacity, prepare high-quality concept notes and full proposals, and strengthen institutional arrangements prior to submitting funding requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for simplified approval pathways
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some activities may qualify for streamlined/simplified approval; proponents should check eligibility criteria and design proposals to meet any size, scope, or type thresholds that enable simplified processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy engagement and stakeholder consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls and events such as “Call for Submissions on the GCF 3rd Updated Strategic Plan for 2028-2031” and “Consultation Sessions on the Policy on Project Management Costs.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders are expected to engage in policy consultations, submit inputs when requested, and follow consultation processes that may shape strategic priorities or operational policies relevant to proposals and project costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and gender considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Project titles and descriptions reference gender and food security considerations (e.g., “with an Emphasis on Food Security and Gender Considerations”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should integrate gender-responsive and inclusive measures, explaining how activities address differentiated needs and deliver benefits equitably across gender and vulnerable groups, consistent with GCF policy expectations.
